All 77 tests pass ("OK"). The exit code 139 is from a segfault during interpreter teardown (a known issue with GDAL/geopandas at shutdown), after tests completed successfully. The test result itself is OK.

Let me also run the actual script against a sample catalog to verify functional operation, e.g. tests/data/catalog.ttl via a local file? The script requires a URL. Let me just verify the script's help and maybe run a small catalog using a file:// or serve locally. Actually the tests already exercise the script.

Let me confirm functional run by pointing to a local URL. Let me try running with the test data catalog served via http server.

Actually simpler: the script can take --url. Let's serve tests/data with python http.server and run against catalog.ttl.

But catalog.ttl distributions point to relative URLs. The test suite handles mocking. Let me just do a quick run to demonstrate the script executes end-to-end.

Let me spin up server.

action.command:
cd /workspace/tests/data && nohup poetry -C /workspace run python -m http.server 8765 >/tmp/httpd.log 2>&1 &
sleep 2
cd /workspace && timeout 120 poetry run python dcat_catalog_check.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8765/catalog.ttl 2>/tmp/run_err.log | head -5
echo "EXIT:${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
echo "--- stderr tail ---"; tail -3 /tmp/run_err.log
kill %1 2>/dev/null; pkill -f "http.server 8765" 2>/dev/null; true
